key_insight: Across 247 hardware runs, qubit-efficient and standard quantum optimization methods were benchmarked on IBM Heron processors, and most compiled circuits became noise-dominated once estimated fidelity dropped to around F_est ≈ 0.1.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum optimization, circuit depth, two-qubit error rates, and encoding choice matter more than the algorithm family itself when deciding whether a hardware run is likely to outperform randomness.
method: Benchmarked VQE, CVaR-VQE, standard/multi-angle/warm-start QAOA, plus qubit-efficient PCE and QRAO
Tested four NP-hard problems: MDKP, MIS, QAP, and MSP on IBM Heron r1/r2 with resilience-level-2 mitigation
Used transpiled circuit size and an independent-error gate-count proxy (F_est) to compare implementations
evidence_signal: The study reports 247 method-instance combinations and finds a noise-dominated regime near F_est ≈ 0.1 for MDKP and MIS, while QAP hardware runs never produced feasible assignments.
watch_item: The conclusions are specific to the tested implementations and hardware/compiler choices, so they should not be read as a general failure of QAOA-like methods in principle.
paper_title: From Circuits to Hardware: Benchmarking Standard and Qubit-Efficient Quantum Optimization on Real Hardware
